In the computer lab of their Guwahati school, Rekha ma'am projected a post onto the screen: a blurry photo, a red headline, and the words SHARE IF YOU'RE ANGRY.
"Before you react," she said, "tell me what this post wants from you."
Binita, who had shared one just like it last week, raised her hand slowly. "It wants me to be angry. And to share it before I check."
"How can you tell?"

Rekha ma'am nodded. "Feeds learn from what makes you stop and react. Anger works best, so they show you more."
